about.a01: The primary reference for governing and developing Quranic software
about.a02: "Discover with confidence. Build with mastery. Share with responsibility."
about.a04: To empower developers and publishers with a safe, curated, standards-governed marketplace for digital Quran resources and apps.
about.a06: To become the world's first standard for trust, accuracy and collaboration in developing Quranic systems and software.
about.a07: What sets RATQ apart from static open directories?
about.a09: We do not merely list a resource; we verify its integrity through Itqan badges, specialised human review and file-safety validation.
about.a11: Clear decision paths for access requests, a tamper-proof audit log, and transparent appeal paths that protect publisher and developer rights.
about.a13: The true owner is the one who manages their assets, issues releases, controls licenses and follows download analytics precisely.
about.a16: The platform supports the whole journey, from discovering a resource to publishing it and keeping its information current.
about.a18: Find libraries, datasets, APIs, and development and research tools through one unified, searchable directory.
about.a20: Review documentation, licenses, versions, attribution and Itqan verification information before choosing the right resource.
about.a22: Publishers can manage restricted resources, review access requests and keep their resource information up to date.
about.a24: Comments, reports and reviews help surface useful resources and spot outdated information and areas needing improvement.
about.a26: Developer pages, API keys, documentation links and integration details make resources easy to use in real projects.
about.a28: Sharia and scholarly accuracy always take precedence over publishing speed.
about.a29: The publisher's right to their resources takes precedence over a user's wish for open access.
about.a30: Governance transparency takes precedence over ease of procedure.
about.a31: Protecting user privacy takes precedence over analytics accuracy and detail.

home.faq1_q: What is the Itqan standard and what sets it apart?
home.faq1_a: The Itqan standard is a multi-level quality governance framework that checks Quranic software resources across 4 layers: technical, security, licensing, and the mandatory approved scholarly and Sharia verification.
home.faq2_q: How do I get an API key for restricted resources?
home.faq2_a: Submit a one-click electronic access request and explain the project's purpose. The publisher reviews and decides on it within the defined SLA, then your secure key is generated.
home.faq3_q: Can Mushaf publishers and publishing houses manage their assets directly?
home.faq3_a: Yes. The platform offers a complete publisher portal to claim resource ownership, release versions, follow developer requests, and get detailed analytics.
home.faq4_q: Does the platform include AI-generated Quranic text?
home.faq4_a: Absolutely not. The platform enforces strict safeguards and rules that prevent AI from generating or guessing Quran text, and every resource is attributed to approved, verified bodies.
home.faq5_q: Is the platform free for developers?
home.faq5_a: Yes. The platform is free for the developer and research community and supports open-source and volunteer projects serving the Book of Allah.

standards.s01: The quality and trust standard for developing Quranic software
standards.s03: A unified technical and scholarly governance framework that guarantees the accuracy of Quranic texts, the stability of code, clear licensing, and the integrity of digital distribution of the Book of Allah.
standards.s06: Complete, self-declared publisher data that meets the minimum of resource name, description, attached license, and linked publisher.
standards.s07: Automatic annual renewal - no human review required
standards.s10: Weekly periodic checks of link integrity, file availability and SHA-256 fingerprint matching, and that the resource is free of errors and malware.
standards.s11: Weekly re-check of links and files
standards.s14: Specialised scholarly review by accredited reviewers confirming correct attribution to the sources of texts and tafsir, plus a full install-and-run test of the software.
standards.s18: The highest level of accreditation: for projects that have proven exceptional stability, regular maintenance, high community ratings (4.5 or more), and complete documentation.
standards.s19: Dual nomination by the standards council - semi-annual check
standards.s20: Badge revocation protocol and public transparency
standards.s21: To preserve the standard's integrity, badges undergo periodic re-verification and are revoked immediately upon persistent failures, scholarly errors, or intellectual property violations. All revocations are announced with full transparency in the public log, and the publisher may appeal within 10 working days.
standards.s22: View the public transparency and revocation log
standards.s52: Standard badges are granted based on the total points achieved, provided the scholarly and Sharia requirements are met 100% without any exception.
standards.s35d: All repository, documentation and file links work and respond with HTTP 200 and no broken redirects.
standards.s36d: Every release carries an exact SHA-256 fingerprint matching the uploaded file to prevent tampering.
standards.s37d: The package contains no malware, unauthorised tracking, or abandoned libraries with critical security vulnerabilities.
standards.s38d: Adherence to SemVer semantic versioning (Major.Minor.Patch), documenting breaking changes in the changelog.
standards.s40d: An accurate Arabic summary of at least 20 characters with a detailed explanation of the nature of the data and target use cases.
standards.s41d: Clear, tested install and call commands for the supported platforms (npm, pip, flutter, REST...).
standards.s42d: An explicit statement of any technical or linguistic limits, usage caps, or external dependencies that require permission.
standards.s45d: Attribution of the Quranic text or tafsir to a declared, documented body (King Fahd Complex for the Printing of the Holy Quran, Tanzil, and others).
standards.s46d: The text is entirely free of any distortion, dropped diacritics, or mixing of the Mushaf's narrations.
standards.s47d: The names of commentators, translators and verifying bodies are documented with complete precision and no ambiguity.
standards.s48d: An absolute and final ban on generating verses or tafsir with generative AI models from memory without direct verification against documented texts.
standards.s50d: An open or custom license is explicitly specified, defining commercial use, modification and redistribution rights.
standards.s51d: Verifying that the resource belongs to the publisher via the institutional domain, official email, or a verified GitHub repository.
